title: READ(...END=900, ERR=999) — twin branches for EOF and read failure
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE LOAD_NEXT(UNIT, X, STATE)
C     END= branches when EOF is reached; ERR= branches on a read
C     failure (malformed number, IO error). Both labels can co-exist
C     in one READ. Translating to a Java try/catch must distinguish
C     EOF (return -1) from IOException -- the legacy code's two
C     paths often resolve to two distinct user-visible behaviours
C     ("end of input" vs "corrupt input").
      IMPLICIT NONE
      INTEGER UNIT, STATE
      REAL    X
      READ (UNIT, *, END=900, ERR=999) X
      STATE = 0
      RETURN
  900 STATE = 1
      RETURN
  999 STATE = 2
      RETURN
      END
notes: END=/ERR= is one of the most common F77 I/O patterns. The 3-way outcome must port to a sealed result enum or an exception+sentinel mix. The spec captures the three paths so the rewrite preserves them.
